mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the negative economic signal.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts by more than 10% in a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased construction activity.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 2% in a month indicates a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors interpret this as a sign of economic strength.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and CPI (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.1% change), it indicates strong consumer demand without inflationary pressures, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% in 1 month and CPIAUCSL changes < 0.1%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 1% and CPIAUCSL changes by less than 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it indicates a potential economic slowdown due to high interest rates, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 2% and GDPC1 YoY growth is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000, signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors interpret this as a sign of economic growth.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month and PAYEMS increases > 200,000
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.
